raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> Kimi-K3 on gfx950 merge queue (all drafts; they land one at a time in this order): 1 #44978 verify argmax + tuned bf16 rows · 2 #44979 MLA prefill · 3 #44980 streaming AttnRes · 4 #44981 MoE prefill · 5 #44982 KDA · 6 #44983 MLA decode prep · 7 #44984 MLA decode epilogue · 8 #44985 LL column tail · 9 #44986 fused all-reduce read · 10 #44987 fused route sort · 11 #44988 split MoE front + bank partials · 12 #44989 MLA q-norm + q_b. Replaces #44547-#44553.

## Motivation

A Kimi-K3 MoE layer at decode sizes runs aiter's biased top-k, two moe_sorting phases and the MXFP8 activation quant
before the experts. The routed output is then copied out of aiter's own output into K3's all-reduce buffer, and the
shared-expert down GEMM into that buffer (`torch.mm(out=)`) lands on hipBLASLt.

## Modifications

Gated on gfx950 with aiter (`SGLANG_USE_AITER`).

- `kimi_k3_route_sort` (`route_sort.cuh`, `route_topk.cuh`): the router top-k (sigmoid + bias selection as aiter's
  topk kernel, renormalized pre-bias weights) and aiter's block-padded moe_sorting layout in one launch for decode
  batches (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSED_ROUTE_SORT_MAX_TOKENS`, 16), with the A8W4 experts' MXFP8 activation quant + scale
  sort folded in up to 8 tokens (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSED_ROUTE_QUANT`). The routes reach aiter's `fused_moe` through
  `moe_sort_handoff`, which aiter's `moe_sorting` / `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort` hooks consume only for the
  exact call they were staged for (aiter's own sort runs otherwise).
- The aiter runner writes the routed output into K3's joint all-reduce buffer (`zero_copy_context`) instead of
  copying it out of its own.
- The shared-expert down GEMM into the all-reduce buffer runs aiter's tuned FlyDSL kernel with `out=` (hipBLASLt
  otherwise).

#44552 also had an opt-in direct route layout (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_MOE_ROUTE_DIRECT_MAX_TOKENS`, off by
default); it measured slower (C1 cycle 16.6 vs 15.7 ms; aiter's A8W4 kernels are tuned for expert-grouped blocks), so
it is not part of this PR.

| New env var | Default |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSED_ROUTE_SORT_MAX_TOKENS` | 16 |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSED_ROUTE_QUANT` | on |

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup for every number below:** 8x MI350X (gfx950, 1000 W), Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE, bf16 attention) at TP8 with EAGLE3
(topk 1, 3 steps, 4 draft tokens), FP8 KV cache, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, aiter's K3 FlyDSL kernels
(`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1`), CUDA graphs for bs 1/2/4/8/16, and an aiter bf16 GEMM table with K3 rows re-tuned on this pod with HBM-resident weights
(`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_BF16`; not part of this PR, it belongs in aiter's model configs). EAGLE3 on K3 needs the
aux-capture commit of #43599, applied locally for these runs. Microbenchmarks rotate their weights through HBM.
Per-feature numbers were measured on the integration branch of this series as each piece landed (Oct 13-14,
earlier `main`). All branches of the series are on `main` 4eb606b2ae (2026-10-17); the kernel tests below ran on this
branch, and the end-to-end checkpoints on that `main` plus the queue up to each slot.

- `test_kimi_k3_route_sort.py` (new): top-k ids, sorted rows, expert blocks and valid counts equal aiter's
  `biased_grouped_topk` + `moe_sorting`, the fused MXFP8 rows equal `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`, NaN /
  saturated logit rows still give 16 distinct experts. On MI350X: 1 passed (6 subtests).
- End to end: GSM8K 200 at each checkpoint of the queue, see below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Route sort at 4 tokens: 6.5 us vs 14.8 (aiter top-k + sort); with the quant 11.6 vs 16.9 us in-server.
- Shared-expert down GEMM with `out=`: 7.0 -> 4.5 us.

### End to end (queue checkpoints)

K3 server built from `main` 4eb606b2ae plus the queue up to each slot, with #43599's aux capture (and #41867 and
#41848 from slot 10 on, which apply only once #44987 is in); C1 decode on a 50K-token cached prefix (500 output tokens)
and GSM8K 200, EAGLE3 as above, measured 2026-10-17. These runs and the previous integration below also set `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_AUTO_KV_SPLITS=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH=128 SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 AITER_MLA_REDUCE_FLYDSL=1`. In bold: the first checkpoint that includes this PR.

| Queue up to | Adds | C1 decode cycle | GSM8K 200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| slot 5 | #44978, #44979, #44980, #44981, #44982 | 21.6 ms\* | 0.995 |
| slot 7 | #44983, #44984 | 19.4 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 9 | #44985, #44986 | 18.6 ms | 0.990 |
| **slot 10** | **#44987, #41867, #41848** | **16.7 ms** | **0.985** |
| slot 11 | #44988 | 15.7 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 12 | #44989 | 15.6 ms | 0.990 |

\* The second of two runs; the first, right after start-up, measured 25.6 ms. The other rows average two runs.

The slot-10 row also adds #41867 and #41848, so not all of the step from slot 9 (18.6 -> 16.7 ms) is this PR's.

The whole series, from the previous integration: the seven earlier drafts (#44547-#44553) merged on `main` b67785153a (this series'
code plus the two opt-in paths it drops, both off by default), with #43599's aux capture, #41867 and #41848; agentic
replay of lightseekorg/agentic-dataset SWE-smith conversations (multi-turn, ~50K-token cached prefixes, 500 output
tokens, greedy), EAGLE3 as above. TokenSpeed (7e2f1deb, same pod, same workload) for reference.

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SGLang, tok/s/user | 217.2 | 156.6 | 114.1 | 73.4 | 43.4 |
| TokenSpeed, tok/s/user | 188.1 | 129.5 | 86.1 | 59.7 | 35.5 |

786/786 requests OK. GSM8K 400: 0.9825 / accept length 3.619. Decode cycle C1 / C4 / C16: 15.8 / 23.2 / 38.9 ms;
agentic turn TTFT (50K cached + 1.9K new tokens) 230-248 ms; uncached 50K-token prefill 3.27 s. The slot-12
checkpoint's C1 cycle (15.6 ms) is in line with it.

## Related

- #43126 (closed) fused radix-4 routing, the MoE sort and the MXFP8 quant on the Quark A4W4 decode path, handing the
  sort to aiter's `fused_moe` (now ROCm/aiter#6484); on MI355X it measured 1-2.6% slower TPOT than separate kernels.
  This PR is the A8W4 path of the stock checkpoint, keeps aiter unchanged, and is faster at the sizes it takes
  (route sort 6.5 vs 14.8 us at 4 tokens, with the quant 11.6 vs 16.9 us in-server; see above).
- ROCm/aiter#6263 fuses the same sort + MXFP8 quant inside aiter; here the router top-k is folded in as well.
- #44294 moves the shared down GEMM to aiter through `tgemm.mm(out=)`, which needs ROCm/aiter#6538 (not in the
  pinned aiter); this PR uses the FlyDSL `out=` the pinned aiter already has.
- The measurements above also had #41867 and #41848 applied.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Fused router top-k + MoE route sort and zero-copy MoE output for decode on gfx950

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,159 @@
+"""Fused Kimi-K3 router top-k + aiter moe_sorting for decode-sized batches (gfx950).
+
+One launch replaces aiter's biased top-k kernel and its two-phase opus
+moe_sorting. The outputs follow aiter.fused_moe.moe_sorting's contract, so
+they can stand in for its return value (see csrc/kimi_k3/route_sort.cuh).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once, load_jit, make_cpp_args
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+MAX_TOKENS: int = 64
+
+
+class RouteSortOutput(NamedTuple):
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor  # [M, topk] fp32
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor  # [M, topk] int32
+    sorted_ids: torch.Tensor
+    sorted_weights: torch.Tensor
+    sorted_expert_ids: torch.Tensor
+    num_valid_ids: torch.Tensor
+    moe_buf: torch.Tensor
+    # Stage-1 MXFP8 activations as aiter.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort
+    # returns them (None unless route_sort was given quant_input).
+    a1: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    a1_scale: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_route_sort_module(
+    num_experts: int,
+    topk: int,
+    bias_dtype: torch.dtype,
+    fuse_quant: bool,
+) -> Module:
+    args = make_cpp_args(num_experts, topk, bias_dtype, fuse_quant)
+    return load_jit(
+        "kimi_k3_route_sort",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["kimi_k3/route_sort.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[("run", f"K3RouteSortKernel<{args}>::run")],
+        extra_cuda_cflags=["-O3"],
+    )
+
+
+def covered(
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor, correction_bias: torch.Tensor, topk: int
+) -> bool:
+    num_tokens, num_experts = router_logits.shape
+    return (
+        0 < num_tokens <= MAX_TOKENS
+        and router_logits.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and router_logits.stride(1) == 1
+        and router_logits.stride(0) % 2 == 0
+        and router_logits.data_ptr() % 4 == 0
+        and correction_bias.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32)
+        and correction_bias.is_contiguous()
+        and num_experts % 128 == 0
+        and num_experts <= 1024
+        and 0 < topk <= 64
+    )
+
+
+def quant_covered(quant_input: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    cols = quant_input.shape[-1]
+    return (
+        quant_input.dim() == 2
+        and quant_input.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and quant_input.stride(1) == 1
+        and quant_input.stride(0) % 8 == 0
+        and quant_input.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+        and cols % 32 == 0
+        and cols // 32 <= 128
+    )
+
+
+def route_sort(
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor,
+    correction_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    topk: int,
+    block_m: int,
+    model_dim: int,
+    moe_buf: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    routed_scaling_factor: float,
+    renormalize: bool,
+    quant_input: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> RouteSortOutput:
+    """Top-k of sigmoid(router_logits) + bias, sorted into aiter's block-padded
+    route layout; moe_buf ([M, model_dim], allocated when None) is zeroed.
+    With quant_input ([M, D] bf16, the routed activations) the stage-1 MXFP8
+    quant + scale sort is fused in as well."""
+    num_tokens, num_experts = router_logits.shape
+    device = router_logits.device
+    # Same sizes as aiter.fused_moe._moe_sorting_impl.
+    max_rows = num_tokens * topk + num_experts * block_m - topk
+    max_blocks = (max_rows + block_m - 1) // block_m
+    max_rows = max_blocks * block_m
+    topk_weights = torch.empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    topk_ids = torch.empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    sorted_ids = torch.empty(max_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    sorted_weights = torch.empty(max_rows, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    sorted_expert_ids = torch.empty(max_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    num_valid_ids = torch.empty(2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if moe_buf is None:
+        moe_buf = torch.empty(

+"""Hand a precomputed aiter moe_sorting result to the next aiter fused_moe call.
+
+A model whose router fuses the top-k with the route sort (Kimi-K3 on gfx950)
+stages the sorted routes here; the aiter runner's moe_sorting hook returns them
+instead of sorting again when the call is the one they were staged for.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+from typing import Iterator, Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+
+class StagedSort(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor
+    block_m: int
+    sorted_ids: torch.Tensor
+    sorted_weights: torch.Tensor
+    sorted_expert_ids: torch.Tensor
+    num_valid_ids: torch.Tensor
+    # zeroed stage-2 accumulation buffer, the runner's zero-copy output
+    moe_buf: torch.Tensor
+    # Optional stage-1 MXFP8 activations for quant_input (the routed rows),
+    # standing in for aiter's fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort.
+    quant_input: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    a1: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    a1_scale: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+
+
+class _Handoff(msgspec.Struct):
+    staged: Optional[StagedSort] = None
+
+
+_handoff = _Handoff()
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def stage(sort: StagedSort) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Publish `sort` for the aiter fused_moe call(s) inside the block."""
+    old, _handoff.staged = _handoff.staged, sort
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _handoff.staged = old
+
+
+def sort_staged() -> bool:
+    return _handoff.staged is not None
+
+
+def active() -> bool:
+    return _handoff.staged is not None
+
+
+def take(
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    block_m: int,
+    output: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    moebuf_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> Optional[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """moe_sorting's return tuple when this call matches the staged sort."""
+    s = _handoff.staged
+    if (
+        s is None
+        or topk_ids.data_ptr() != s.topk_ids.data_ptr()
+        or topk_ids.shape != s.topk_ids.shape
+        or block_m != s.block_m
+        or output is None
+        or output.data_ptr() != s.moe_buf.data_ptr()
+        or output.shape != s.moe_buf.shape
+        or moebuf_dtype != s.moe_buf.dtype
+    ):
+        return None
+    return (
+        s.sorted_ids,
+        s.sorted_weights,
+        s.sorted_expert_ids,
+        s.num_valid_ids,
+        s.moe_buf,
+    )
+
+
+def take_quant(
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+    sorted_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    num_valid_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    token_num: int,
+) -> Optional[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """The stage-1 (a1, a1_scale) staged with the sort, when this quant call is
+    the one it was staged for."""
+    s = _handoff.staged
+    if (
+        s is not None
+        and s.a1 is not None
+        and s.quant_input is not None
+        and input.data_ptr() == s.quant_input.data_ptr()
+        and input.shape == s.quant_input.shape
+        and input.stride() == s.quant_input.stride()
+        and sorted_ids.data_ptr() == s.sorted_ids.data_ptr()
+        and token_num == s.a1.shape[0]
+    ):
+        return s.a1, s.a1_scale
+    return None

+"""The gfx950 Kimi-K3 fused router top-k + MoE route sort against aiter's chain."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+# backend-specific: the route sort hands aiter's gfx950 A8W4 MoE its routes.
+register_amd_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+# Kimi-K3 TP8: 896 experts, top-16, latent 3584, hidden 7168, up to 8 bank rows.
+E, K, LATENT, H, NB = 896, 16, 3584, 7168, 9
+BLOCK_M = 32
+
+
+def _routes(out, num_tokens):
+    """{(token, slot): (row, weight)} over the valid rows; padding rows carry weight 0."""
+    pad = (K << 24) | num_tokens
+    ids, weights = out.sorted_ids.cpu(), out.sorted_weights.cpu()
+    routes = {}
+    for row in range(int(out.num_valid_ids[0])):
+        v = int(ids[row])
+        if v == pad:
+            assert float(weights[row]) == 0.0
+            continue
+        routes[(v & 0xFFFFFF, v >> 24)] = (row, float(weights[row]))
+    return routes
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_gfx95_supported(), "gfx950 route sort")
+class TestKimiK3RouteSort(CustomTestCase):
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_matches_aiter_topk_sort_and_quant(self):
+        """On router logits strided inside the fused front's output, one launch gives
+        aiter's biased top-k and moe_sorting (ids, sorted rows, expert blocks, valid
+        counts), a zeroed moe_buf and fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort's
+        activations; a NaN or saturated logits row still yields 16 distinct experts."""
+        import aiter
+        from aiter import biased_grouped_topk
+        from aiter.fused_moe import moe_sorting
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.kimi_k3_route_sort import route_sort
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(2)
+        bias = (torch.randn(E, generator=g, device="cuda") * 0.05).bfloat16()
+        for num_tokens in (1, 4, 16):
+            front = torch.randn(
+                num_tokens, 1536 + E + LATENT, generator=g, device="cuda"
+            )
+            front = (front * 2).bfloat16()
+            logits, routed = front[:, 1536 : 1536 + E], front[:, 1536 + E :]
+            want_w = torch.empty(num_tokens, K, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+            want_ids = torch.empty(num_tokens, K, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+            biased_grouped_topk(logits, bias, want_w, want_ids, 1, 1, True, 1.0)
+            sorted_ids, _, sorted_experts, num_valid, _ = moe_sorting(
+                want_ids, want_w, E, LATENT, torch.bfloat16, BLOCK_M
+            )
+            buf = torch.full((num_tokens, LATENT), 5.0, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+            got = route_sort(
+                logits, bias, topk=K, block_m=BLOCK_M, model_dim=LATENT, moe_buf=buf,
+                routed_scaling_factor=1.0, renormalize=True, quant_input=routed,
+            )  # fmt: skip
+            want_a1, _ = aiter.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort(
+                routed, sorted_ids, num_valid, num_tokens, K, BLOCK_M

+def _row_scales(scales: torch.Tensor, row: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The e8m0 group scales of a sorted row in aiter's shuffled layout."""
+    n_pad = scales.shape[1]
+    flat = scales.flatten()
+    idx = [
+        (row // 32 * n_pad) * 32
+        + (g // 8) * 256
+        + (g % 4) * 64
+        + (row % 16) * 4
+        + (g % 8) // 4 * 2
+        + (row % 32) // 16
+        for g in range(LATENT // 32)
+    ]
+    return flat[idx]
